tldr: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol on June 26 as its next flagship, pairing coding, science, and cybersecurity gains with its most advanced safety stack. A day later the family shipped only to a restricted trusted-partner tier, alongside an unrelated Anthropic release the same day.
whats_new: GPT-5.6 — Luna, Terra, and Sol — reached general availability on July 9, with OpenAI's own launch post landing the same day as Simon Willison's independent GA writeup.
why_it_matters: The GA move ends the two-week restricted-partner window and adds a three-tier lineup (Luna/Terra/Sol) with per-tier pricing, so integrations built against the preview or partner tier should re-check access and re-evaluate cost/latency against the new tiers before defaulting to the largest model.

status.detail: Preview (Jun 26) -> restricted partner access (Jun 27) -> general availability (Jul 9).

beats.headline: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol with an upgraded safety stack
beats.summary: First look at the next-generation model, ahead of any public release.

beats.headline: Family ships to trusted partners only, not the general public
Luna, Terra, and Sol open to everyone with tiered per-token pricing
beats.summary: Luna prices at $1/$6 per 1M input/output tokens as the smallest of the three sizes.

open_questions: What are Terra's and Sol's exact per-token prices relative to Luna's $1/$6?
Does GA access carry the same safety commitments OpenAI described in the June 26 preview?
take_for_builders: If you were on the restricted GPT-5.6 tier, re-check your access and quota now that GA is open, and benchmark Luna's $1/$6-per-1M-token tier against your current model before defaulting to Sol for cost-sensitive agent loops.
